question.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ what are the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

- From the matrix $C=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -(-2) & 4\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that $\text{Re}(\lambda )=4$ and $\text{Im}(\lambda )=-2.$ So, our eigenvalue is

$$
\lambda =4+(-2)\text{i}=4-2\text{i}.
$$

- From the matrix $P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}],$ we deduce that our corresponding eigenvector is

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2+3\text{i} \\ -4+(-1)\text{i}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2+3\text{i} \\ -4-\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of $\lambda ,$ and the second eigenvector must be the complex conjugate of $v.$

Therefore, our eigenvalues and eigenvectors are 

$$
\lambda =4∓2\text{i},\,v=[\begin{aligned}2\pm 3\text{i} \\ -4∓\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$
